title: Dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and for $x\in X$ let $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be its local ring at $x$. Then the Krull dimension $\dim X$ of the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals $\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, where $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the Krull dimension of the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and the supremum is taken in $\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ (both sides are $-\infty$ when $X$ is empty).

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 04MU (label lemma-dimension, line 1233), equality of (1) and (2); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (04MU,properties-lemma-dimension)

proof.text: Unfold topologicalKrullDim [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A scheme is quasi-sober and T0 [lem-sc-scheme-sober], so Mathlib irreducibleSetEquivPoints identifies its irreducible closed subsets with its points in the specialization order. Apply Order.krullDim_eq_of_orderIso to this order isomorphism.

Apply Mathlib Order.krullDim_eq_iSup_coheight to express the Krull dimension of the specialization order as the supremum of the coheights of its points. This theorem includes the empty case, where the supremum is bottom.

For every point x, Mathlib ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] identifies the Krull dimension of the stalk with the coheight of x. Taking the supremum over x (iSup_congr) gives Scheme.dim = topologicalKrullDim X, since Scheme.dim is definitionally the supremum of these stalk dimensions.
